title: GraphReFly
description: The graph you see is the system that runs. GraphReFly keeps state, computation, effects, and inspection in one executable graph.
public_summary: One executable graph for state, computation, consequences, and inspection.

hero.meta: Software should be able to explain its consequences.
headline: The graph you see,
the system that runs.
hero.body: State, computation, and effects live in one executable graph. Changes move through declared relationships, related branches settle coherently, and humans and agents inspect the same system that actually ran.
hero.category: Executable reactive graphs for changing software.

example.heading: Change one input. Watch its consequences move.
example.intro: Follow one cause through the paths it affects, then watch those paths settle into one shared result.
example.problem: If the total publishes too early, the customer can see new tax combined with old shipping.
example.solution: The address change moves through declared dependencies. The shared result waits for every registered path to settle, then publishes one coherent answer.

diagram.heading: One change moves through every affected branch
diagram.aria_label: Conceptual walkthrough of a delivery address change settling through affected branches

problem.heading: Your code runs one system. Your team reasons about another.
problem.body: State lives in stores. Control flow hides in callbacks and queues. Causality is reconstructed from logs. Documentation describes a system that may no longer exist. Every change asks people and agents to rebuild the same mental model again.
problem.without: Code, workflow state, diagrams, logs, and AI context drift apart.
problem.with: Shared state and computation remain connected through the graph that actually executes them.

reasons.heading: Declare the relationships once. Let the running system preserve them.

items.title: The topology is truthful
items.body: Every visible edge represents a real dependency. If computation depends on something, that relationship belongs in the graph.
items.benefit: Review the dependency that executes, not a diagram that only resembles it.

items.title: Consequences stay coherent
items.body: A change can fan out through several branches without publishing a shared result from half-old, half-new inputs.
items.benefit: Let the protocol settle shared results instead of rebuilding coordination by hand.

items.title: Context follows dependency
items.body: Each node works from its declared inputs. People and agents can focus on the relevant path instead of loading one global workflow state.
items.benefit: Give each participant the relevant path without loading one global workflow state.

inspection.heading: Ask the graph that actually ran.
inspection.intro: GraphReFly exposes read-only views over the executable graph, not a second control plane.

items.name: describe()
items.body: See the live topology, dependencies, status, values, and metadata.

items.name: observe()
items.body: Watch messages move through a node, subtree, or graph.

items.name: profile()
items.body: When supported and enabled by the package, measure where computation invokes, emits, resolves, and fails.

boundary.heading: Keep outside work honest.
boundary.body: Network calls, models, workers, files, and remote graphs do not share the graph’s timing or failure model. Keep them behind explicit boundaries, then return their outcomes as named facts.
boundary.callout: External execution can stay private. Decision-relevant state must return to the graph.

shared_truth.heading: One executable truth for humans and agents.
shared_truth.body: An agent should not need a full repository dump or a manually maintained workflow description to understand one graph input change. The graph already identifies the relevant runtime state, dependencies, and downstream paths.
shared_truth.note: GraphReFly is not an AI-only library. AI makes the cost of hidden state and duplicated mental models impossible to ignore.

evidence.heading: GraphReFly provides the causal evidence. Humans and agents explain it.
evidence.body: Live topology, current values, and ordered runtime events give explanations a factual starting point. GraphReFly is building richer causal linkage across runtime occurrences, code, decisions, and verification.

progress.heading: From explainable structure to accountable software.

items.label: Available today
items.body: Executable graph topology, declared dependencies, coherent waves, graph-visible shared state, and read-only inspection surfaces.

items.label: Building
items.body: Runtime causal linkage, richer Canvas visualization, and connections between graph, code, decisions, tests, and evidence.

items.label: Direction
items.body: Durable execution and recovery, so the same visible model can eventually explain, control, and answer for what happens next.

adoption.heading: Start with one result your team does not understand.
adoption.body: Replace one bounded piece of coordination glue: a derived decision, policy path, fan-out/fan-in calculation, or agent step.
adoption.note: You do not need to rewrite the whole system to stop maintaining two versions of one part of it.

packages.heading: Use the language your team already works in.
packages.intro: The graph model is shared. Installation, examples, and exact APIs live with each language package.

title: Why GraphReFly
description: Why executable graphs reduce model drift between code, state, diagrams, logs, and AI context.
public_summary: Why the representation people inspect should participate in execution.

hero.heading: Software becomes hard to change when it has more than one version of the truth.
hero.body: Code, workflow state, diagrams, logs, and AI context drift apart. GraphReFly makes one executable graph the shared source of truth for state, computation, and consequences.

sections.heading: Your system already produces plenty of information. It does not produce one coherent explanation.
body: Stores show values, traces show calls, diagrams show intent, and AI summarizes whatever context it receives. The hard question is which representation still matches the system that actually ran.

rows: Why they changed and what depends on them
Current topology, omitted events, and domain meaning
Whether that context is current, complete, or authoritative
External evidence remains explicit rather than silently assumed

sections.callout: Adding another representation does not solve model drift. The representation has to participate in execution.

sections.heading: It is the system.
body: Visible edges are real dependencies: shared state enters as nodes, computation follows those edges, and effects stay connected to their causes. Private machinery can remain abstracted, but the facts and relationships that determine behavior cannot.
sections.callout: Abstraction without a second version of the truth.

sections.heading: Every calculation can be correct while the result is still wrong.
body: An address change fans out through tax, shipping, availability, and the order total. If the shared result publishes before those paths settle, every function can be locally correct while the customer sees a globally wrong answer.

example.label: Delivery address
example.without: Application code manually invalidates results, tracks pending branches, and decides when enough callbacks have completed. That coordination becomes a second workflow hidden beside the calculations.
example.with: Within one graph update, the address change moves through declared dependencies. Affected branches become dirty before new values settle. Their shared downstream result waits until the registered paths have settled, then publishes one coherent answer.

sections.callout: One change. Many consequences. One coherent result.
sections.after: The same pattern appears wherever several facts converge into one decision, view, policy, plan, or agent result.

sections.heading: Give each participant what it depends on, not one global state and not a disconnected fragment.
body: Global state makes every consumer appear to depend on everything, while hand-built context creates another stale copy. A declared graph lets each participant inspect the path it actually depends on without losing its place in the larger causal structure.
sections.callout: Smaller context, without a second version of the truth.
sections.after: AI makes the tradeoff obvious: it needs less context, but that context must still match execution.

sections.heading: GraphReFly provides the causal evidence. Humans and agents explain it.
body: Live topology, current values, and ordered runtime events show what exists, what changed, and where the change moved. Humans, tools, or models can explain that evidence, but the explanation remains checkable against the graph.
sections.callout: The explanation may be generated. The evidence should not be.

sections.heading: Keep different timing and failure modes honest.
body: Files, networks, workers, models, databases, and remote graphs have timing and failure modes that do not behave like synchronous graph computation. Keep that work behind explicit boundaries, then return its requests, outcomes, status, and consequences as graph-visible facts.
sections.callout: Private machinery must not become hidden shared truth.
sections.after: Durable execution and recovery can later integrate at the same boundary without creating another authoritative workflow model.

sections.heading: What GraphReFly changes

example.without: The real system emerges from code, callbacks, stores, queues, logs, and undocumented conventions. Developers and agents reconstruct it differently each time.
example.with: Declared topology carries real computation. Shared state stays connected to its consumers. Related consequences settle coherently. Inspection reads from the same graph the application runs.

sections.callout: GraphReFly does not eliminate code, storage, logs, or external runtimes. It gives them one executable causal structure to connect through.

sections.heading: Start with the result your team understands least.
body: Start where connected change already creates coordination glue or repeated confusion.
bullets: a derived decision fed by several facts
a policy path that is difficult to explain
a read model maintained through manual invalidation
an agent step surrounded by validation, fallback, and review
a subsystem whose diagram and implementation no longer agree
sections.callout: Replace one shadow workflow with one executable graph. Then decide whether the surrounding system should follow.

coda.heading: Today, software produces consequences faster than people can understand them.
coda.body: We believe software should be able to explain, and eventually answer for, what it changes.
